not_yet_declared: the runner image (docker/minimal/): how a corpus runs it is documented in README.md under 'Running it for a corpus' and nothing renders it from this file yet
the tagging scheme a consumer pins (TC-06): this file names the repository and how to ask the build for a tag, and says nothing about what a tag promises

editor.what_it_is: code-server with the runtimes a corpus declares, served to a browser on loopback

image.why_no_registry: this component has no remote and is never pushed; a consumer builds the image from this checkout and pins the tag the build prints
image.compose_value: ${EDITOR_IMAGE:?build it with docker/editor/build.py and pin the tag it prints}

not_carried.sqlite: the runner installs it from Debian's packages into /usr/bin, and the editor copies only /opt and /usr/local out of the runner

runs_as.set_to: the uid:gid that owns the mounted sources on the host
runs_as.why: a container that runs as root writes root-owned files into the mounted sources, and the reader can then never edit their own repository
runs_as.how: the base image's fixuid repairs the passwd record and the ownership of the home directory for whatever uid the consumer ran it as; the editor's entrypoint runs it before it seeds anything, so a uid other than 1000 starts

workspace.why: the workspace ROOT is not in the image, so docker would create it root-owned and no build could write .gradle/, .kotlin/ or build/ into it; a named volume there is root-owned for the same reason. A tmpfs is world-writable, holds only those scratch directories, and is discarded with the container. The source binds sit inside it

mounts.purpose: the corpus's sources, and nothing else: not the repository, not $HOME
code-server's user data: the settings the entrypoint seeds once, and the reader's own edits
the Gradle user home the entrypoint seeds from the prime when it is empty; omit it when gradle is not declared
the Maven local repository the entrypoint seeds from the prime when it is empty; omit it when maven is not declared

ports.why: an unencrypted IDE with a shell. 0.0.0.0 offers it to every machine that can reach this host

environment.name: PASSWORD
environment.note: there is deliberately no default: the IDE must never start unauthenticated

environment.name: GRADLE_USER_HOME
environment.note: explicit rather than derived from $HOME, so the seeded cache and the tool agree

command_notes.bind_addr: 0.0.0.0 INSIDE the container only, which is the container's own interface; the loopback restriction is the ports entry's host_bind
command_notes.replaces_cmd: a compose command: replaces the image's CMD outright, and the image re-declares ENTRYPOINT and CMD so nothing the base bakes is appended to it
command_notes.extensions_dir: the extensions are installed into the image, not onto a volume, so an image upgrade carries them

healthcheck.why_this_interpreter: code-server's own node, which every declared set carries; a set without python has no python3 and a set without node has no node on PATH
healthcheck.ordering: a consumer whose own service creates one of the bind sources gates this one on it with depends_on: <service>: condition: service_healthy, so the editor starts after the directory exists

editor.why_no_docker_socket: spec 8.3: the Docker socket is never mounted into a serving process, not behind a flag and not only locally. This is an IDE with a shell published on a port
editor.why_restart_no: an IDE with a shell comes up when the reader asks for it, not on every boot
